summary: This Snorble company article explains that fear of the dark is common in children and calls the fear nyctophobia. It covers possible causes, including ancestral predator risk, traumatic experiences, unexplained noises, and frightening media. It then offers parenting strategies such as talking openly about the fear, using security objects, nightlights, and relaxation training, and presents the Snorble smart companion as a nightlight and bedtime aid.
one_line: A parenting article on why children fear the dark, with tips such as security objects, nightlights and bedtime relaxation, promoting the Snorble smart companion.
key_facts: Fear of the dark is called nyctophobia, a term that comes from the Greek word for night.
Generally, children begin to fear the dark around age two.
The fear of the dark can last from a few weeks to a few years, depending on genetic makeup, traumatic events, or underlying issues such as ADD, PTSD, and OCD.
The article says that ancestors who slept out in the open found darkness very dangerous because predators roamed the night.
A person who has a troubling or traumatic experience in the dark is more likely to develop a fear of it.
Fear of the dark in toddlers and preschoolers can be brought on by noises they hear when the lights go out, especially when they have no idea where the noises are coming from.
Kids are highly influenced by what they see, so walking in on an older sibling watching a horror movie could turn into nyctophobia.
Triggers for nyctophobic children include getting ready for bed, walking into dark places even during the day such as movie theaters or basements, and watching shows with nighttime scenes.
The article advises against ignoring or teasing a child about the fear, since this may magnify it; it suggests saying, "Tell me what's scaring you so we can talk about it."
A security object like a blanket or stuffed animal can help children feel more relaxed and secure during the night.
Nightlights can help children get over their fear of the dark as long as they are not exposed to bright blue light while trying to sleep.
Yoga, meditation, and reflection are described as great ways to train a child to relax before bed.
Snorble offers yoga, meditation, and reflection as part of the Bedtime Experience wind-down component.
The product is listed at $299 with limited quantities available.
The article is dated December 13, 2022, and is published by Snorble Incorporated.
